title: Proximity and Knowledge Spillovers: Evidence from the Introduction of New Airline Routes
year_note: frame.csv lists 2021 (submission id); published volume 70 issue 11 (2024).
eligible_reason: Figure 3 (an_Figures.do line 102) is an unstacked, binned event study: reghdfe lognumcit_3yr on relative-time indicators before_treat3, before_treat2, before_treat1, after_treat0, after_treat1, after_treat2, after_treat3 (>= +3) with directed-CBSA-pair (ID) and year fixed effects, no controls, clustered by pair. The binary treatment is a one-time reduction of at least 1.5 hours in the pair's travel time (new flight connection), switching on at pair-specific years; pairs whose travel time never changed are never-treated controls. This satisfies every rule in PROTOCOL.md Section 2. All tabled specifications (Tables 3-8) use the continuous log travel time loghrs (or its lead/lag and interactions) and are not eligible.
design_notes: Balanced panel of 110,998 directed CBSA pairs (ID) x years 1980-2010 (Data.dta; 3-year citation window). Main tables: reghdfe log(1 + three-year citations from cit_cbsa to ref_cbsa) on loghrs (log one-way travel time in hours, continuous) with absorb(i.year#i.cit_cbsa i.year#i.ref_cbsa ID), cluster(ID); Table 3 cols 1-2 use absorb(year cit_cbsa ref_cbsa) with logdist and size controls; col 4 adds loghrs_lag1 and loghrs_lead1. Tables 4-8: heterogeneity by citation source, distance/absorptive-capacity/complexity quartiles, alternative windows, knowledge creation outcomes, inventor mobility, period and internet-penetration splits. Figure 3 construction (an_Figures.do lines 34-91): flag within-pair changes in loghrs; keep pairs with no change (numchge == 0) or exactly one change that is a decrease (numdecr == 1 & numchge == 1); yrchge = year of the change; timechge = hours change; event-time dummies relative to yrchge; estimation sample timechge <= -1.5 | timechge == 0. Omitted reference: treated-pair years at t <= -4 plus all never-treated pair-years. an_Figures.log (run on the real Data.dta) reports N = 2,588,996 and 83,516 clusters.
main_or_robustness_note: The continuous loghrs specification is the paper's main design; the binary event study (Figure 3) supports the dynamics/pre-trend argument.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Pair-specific change years between 1981 and 2010 (up to 30 cohorts); the exact distribution is not recoverable because the shipped Data_synthetic.dta replaces all variable values with random draws.

specs.outcome: lognumcit_3yr = log(1 + numcit_3yr), three-year backward citations from cit_cbsa to ref_cbsa
specs.treatment_var: before_treat3 before_treat2 before_treat1 after_treat0 after_treat1 after_treat2 after_treat3 (relative-time indicators; after_treat3 bins t >= 3)
specs.treatment_definition: treated pair = exactly one within-pair travel-time change over 1980-2010, a reduction of at least 1.5 hours (timechge <= -1.5), occurring in yrchge; control pairs have no change (timechge == 0). Treatment is absorbing from yrchge onward (gen after = year - yrchge >= 0, line 90).
specs.unit_var: ID (directed CBSA pair cit_cbsa x ref_cbsa)
specs.sample_condition: keep if numchge==0 | (numdecr==1 & numchge==1) (line 51); then if timechge<=-1.5 | timechge==0
specs.data_file: Data.dta (NOT shipped; Data_synthetic.dta is a random subsample with randomly generated values)
specs.notes: Static TWFE counterpart would be reghdfe lognumcit_3yr after, a(year ID) cluster(ID) on the same sample (after defined at line 90 but not estimated).

specs.exclusion_reason: continuous treatment (log travel time); time-invariant distance control
specs.treatment_definition: log one-way travel time in hours between the CBSA pair in year t
specs.notes: Columns 1-2 (lines 122, 124) use absorb(year cit_cbsa ref_cbsa) with size controls; column 4 (line 128) adds loghrs_lag1 and loghrs_lead1.

specs.outcome: log citation counts by source (T4), by subsample/quartile (T5), knowledge-creation outcomes (T6), dmmove/dmcollab (T7), period and internet splits (T8)
specs.treatment_var: loghrs (continuous); T8 cols 4-5 interact loghrs with logband / dyadic internet categories
specs.fe: i.year#i.cit_cbsa + i.year#i.ref_cbsa + ID (T6 cols 1-3: i.year#i.ref_cbsa + cit_cbsa + ID)

data_access_note: README: Data_synthetic.dta 'contains a random sample taken from the Data.dta, with the actual values of variables replaced by randomly generated variables ... the output produced by using Data_synthetic.dta does not mirror the actual results.' Raw inputs include non-redistributable ER-586 airline segment data (1977-1989), SDC Platinum and Compustat Segment; T-100, PatentsView, FCC Form 477 and HUD crosswalks are public. Reconstruction code (cr_traveltime.do, cr_patent.do) is shipped.
data_files: Data_synthetic.dta (1,031,975 rows x 55 vars; synthetic values)
replication_feasible_note: Requires the authors' Data.dta (or rebuilding it, which needs the licensed ER-586, SDC and Compustat Segment inputs). Author outreach needed.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text; the OpenAlex abstract is empty). Figure 3's main-text status inferred from the README ('an_Figures.do ... generates all Figures'); confirm against the published PDF. The log file an_Figures.log contains the real-data Figure 3 coefficients recorded under published_estimates.
